text:
jules: Noticed a persistent cluster of tiny free GPU fragments in ap-northeast1 over the past 3h. Pod fit failures up, preempt churn too.
owen: Yup. Trace shows scheduler prefers dense packing across heterogeneous GPUs; leftover small islands are useless.
li: Any customer impact?
jules: A few training jobs reported longer queue times; internal batch pipelines delayed ~2-4min.
maya: Could we bias the scheduler to try warm-pools first when a small-frag island exists? That would reduce reshuffle preempts.
owen: Idea: introduce a soft-node-taint on reserved nodes (effect=PreferNoSchedule) + preferWarmPoolScore in scheduling scores. Quick experiment for a single az.
li: Sounds good. How to toggle?
owen: Patch plan: 1) label reserved nodes: kubectl label node <node> reserved=yes 2) add a soft taint: `kubectl taint nodes <node> gpu_reserve=soft:PreferNoSchedule` 3) add scheduler scoring override in configmap for ap-northeast1 cohort.
jules: Can we do tolerations on low-prio namespaces instead of touching node taints? less global impact.
maya: Tolerations help new pods land, but the scheduling preference still needs weighting. We'll do both: tolerations + scoring.
infra-bot: [runbook] scheduling-experiment: cohort=ap-northeast1a, duration=45m, owner=owen.
owen: here's the config patch I plan to apply (dry-run first):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gpu-scheduler-config
  namespace: kube-system
data:
  preferWarmPoolScore: "50"
  group: "ap-northeast1a-experiment"
```
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system apply -f gpu-scheduler-config-patch.yaml --dry-run=server
```
li: Also propose scaling warm-pool in that AZ by +15 to absorb small pods quickly.
jules: Go ahead but limit to low-priority namespaces (ns: spot-batch).
maya: I'll run the warm-pool scale and namespace toleration patch now.
```bash
kubectl -n infra-scale scale deploy/warm-pool-apn --replicas=55 # from 40
kubectl -n spot-batch patch deployment --all -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu_reserve","operator":"Exists","effect":"PreferNoSchedule","tolerationSeconds":2700}]}}}}'
```
owen: Doing dry-run apply of scheduler config, then a gradual live apply to 10% of schedulers (canary).
infra-bot: [info] warm-pool scale requested by maya. id=r-12ac.
jules: Monitor metrics: fit_failures, preempt_rate, pod_start_time. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/sched/scheduler-health?panel=frag_islands
li: If preempt_rate drops by >30% within 20m, keep for 45m. If not, rollback immediately.
maya: Warm-pool scaled to 55, tolerations applied. Seeing more pods start.
owen: Applied configmap canary to 10% of schedulers. Dry-run looked good.
infra-bot: [metric] ap-northeast1 preempt_rate delta=-12% (10m).
jules: Early sign of improvement. Keep watching for 20m.
li: Any long-term thoughts? heuristic to prefer warm-pool fill, and make reserved nodes soft by default during peak load windows.
owen: Agree. We'll capture results and write an RFC for an adaptive scoring policy.
maya: Adding follow-ups: 1) run 45m experiment 2) collect detailed allocation traces (owen) 3) test scheduler scoring on staging (li) 4) RFC draft (jules).
jules: Thanks team. If things regress, revert warm-pool and remove canary config.
infra-bot: [alert] scheduling-experiment complete: result=successish, next=analyze_traces.
